figures.caption: Figure 1: Visualization of vision encoder behavior under standard fine-tuning and our method, and the changes induced by the patch-level SIG regularizer.

Table 2: Mechanism analysis on CholecT50. For image encoders, No IDM&FWM denotes the CLIP4Clip-style temporal baseline, No Patch-level SIG retains IDM/FWM but removes the patch-level regularizer, and With Patch-level SIG denotes the full model. PR, entropy rank, and d90 are computed from δt = st+1−st; lower values indicate more concentrated transition variance. Higher IoUnorm indicates stronger Instrument-tissues interaction region grounding. Video encoders are Standard-FT references, and dashes denote unreported transition statistics.

Figure 4: Per-bin CH→mAP trajectories (da = 128, triplet mAP). Test frames are split into five CH quintile bins (z-scored, pooled per pair); each arrow joins the mean CH (x) and triplet mAPIVT (y) of the two models (start hollow, end filled), bins colored dark→ bright for low→ high CH. CH is over the Instrument-tissues interaction region object classes plus one background class, so it rewards objects separating from each other and from background. Columns: ViT-L, DINOv2, SurgeNet. (a) baseline (no IDM/FWM)→ LAViFiT (blue); (b) LAViFiT without PatchSIG→ LAViFiT (orange). Up-right motion = higher separability and recognition; (c) baseline (no IDM/FWM).→ LAViFiT (green) without Patch-SIG. Up-right motion = higher separability and recognition

Figure 5: Effect of the action-token dimension da on CholecT50. Each panel plots mAP versus da ∈{64,...,1024} for the three encoders (ViT-L, DINOv2, SurgeNet), for the triplet metric and the instrument/verb/target components.

Figure 6: Effect of the action dimension da on representation quality for ViT-L, DINOv2-L, and SurgeNet-L. (a) Subspace-grounding IoU and (b) CH score versus da. The grounding IoU is computed from the top-r eigenvectors of the transition covariance with r=128fixed for all models. Each panel uses its owny-scale to make per-encoder trends visible.

Figure 3: PCA-RGB visualizations of encoders trained with and without our latent action framework on (a) CholecT50 [43] and (b) ProstaTD [10]. All variants of our method are trained with IDM, FWM, and patch-level SIGReg. V-JEPA2 and V-JEPA2.1 figures are visualized using tublet tokens.

Figure 2: Overview of LAViFiT. The vision encoder maps a surgical clip to state tokens, while the IDM compresses consecutive-state changes into latent actions and the FWM predicts the next state using a stop-gradient target. Frameand patch-level SIGReg prevent collapse, and the state-action sequence is aggregated and the aggregation token aligned with instrument-verb-target text embeddings.
Table 3: Per-component learning rates for each vision encoder. Encoder is the vision backbone’s rate. Weight decay is shared across all groups.

Table 1: Main results and ablations on CholecT50 and ProstaTD. We report instrument, verb, target, and triplet mAP. ProstaTD results are mean ± standard deviation across the 5 cross-validation folds; CholecT50 uses a single run. † and ‡ denote image and video encoders, and ∗ denotes our reimplementation of VL-JEPA. SIGp is the patch-level SIG regularizer. Removing SIGp and IDM/FWM yields a CLIP4Clip-style baseline [6]. The no-action-token variant is evaluated only at inference.
